mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate signals a shift towards accommodative monetary policy, leading to increased borrowing and spending, which in turn drives up the S&P 500 over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 50% of instances where the federal funds rate decreases.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the unemployment rate above 5% triggers a slowdown in consumer spending, leading to decreased demand for goods and services, and ultimately resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 40% of instances where the unemployment rate exceeds 5%.

mechanism_narrative: A joint increase in housing starts and retail sales signals a strong consumer demand environment, leading to increased economic growth and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 30% of instances where both housing starts and retail sales increase.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production signals a decrease in the supply of goods and services, leading to increased prices and decreased economic growth, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances where industrial production decreases.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate above 4% triggers a decrease in borrowing and spending, leading to decreased economic growth and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 50% of instances where the federal funds rate exceeds 4%.

mechanism_narrative: A joint decrease in the unemployment rate and increase in payroll employment signals a strong labor market environment, leading to increased economic growth and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 30% of instances where both the unemployment rate decreases and payroll employment increases.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in GDP signals an increase in aggregate demand, leading to increased economic growth and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 50% of instances where GDP increases.

mechanism_narrative: A joint increase in industrial production and decrease in unemployment rate signals a strong supply environment, leading to increased economic growth and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 30% of instances where both industrial production increases and the unemployment rate decreases.
